A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpaceVista dataset, benchmark and model. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison. Revised benchmark counts limit direct performance comparisons but do not prevent comparing the documents.

before.justification: v1 reports original SpaceVista evaluations, component ablations, training diagnostics, dataset quality assessments and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and ablations and adds results on unusually sized objects from Guinness World Records.

M1.justification: The data-construction pipeline, DINOv3 feature fusion, routed LoRA-like scale experts, progressive rewards and GRPO training remain unchanged. The newly specified semantic embedding model and explanation of expert training document implementation rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a Guinness World Records test extending ordinary size variation to record-breaking objects, using over 50 images and size questions. The original training domains, 19 task types and five principal benchmarks remain; removing detailed benchmark tables does not remove those benchmarks from evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds VLM-3R to the SpaceVista-Bench comparison. Conversely, removing v1 Tables D16-D19 removes extensive benchmark-specific comparator sets, including VideoLLaMA3-7B and VideoChat-R1 on STI-Bench and NVILA models on MMSI-Bench. The aggregate comparison in Table 2 retains its comparator membership.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendix B.3.7 revise SpaceVista-Bench from approximately 3,000 questions over 500 videos to 1,600 over 300. New experiments introduce a size-only reference subset for GWR, a vanilla SFT+RL control and a six-expert configuration; the 32B scaling experiment is removed. These are substantial changes to reported evaluation settings, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds the GWR size-bias stress test and expands component analysis with an RL control and six-expert failure case. It removes the reward-convergence analysis, expert-activation visualizations, model-size scaling study and some dataset-distribution analyses. The earlier seen/unseen-object, balanced-scene and 2.5D robustness analyses are retained under reorganized appendix sections.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance. Both retain the qualitative annotation marking unusual variation between human annotators; changed agreement percentages do not constitute a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes SpaceVista-Bench SFT/RL scores from 34.5/36.7 to 35.4/39.2; the revised benchmark counts prevent treating these as confirmed same-setting gains. Expert-count results change, GWR results are added, and detailed external-benchmark and scaling results disappear. Training-data human-check rates also change: route planning 53% to 69%, navigation 63% to 67%, and obstacles 67% to 74%.

T1.justification: The feature-fusion, expert-routing, progressive-reward, GRPO and depth-consistency equations remain mathematically equivalent. Combining and renumbering equations introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an automated all-scale dataset, a physically grounded benchmark and a scale-aware reasoning model with competitive performance. Condensed wording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The earlier interpretation that increasing expert count improves performance becomes a non-monotonic account invoking router load imbalance. Appendix C.4 adds distinctions between category and size shifts, limitations exposed by GWR, and depth/scale-prior explanations. v2 also drops the 99% benchmark-accuracy assertion and adds an explanation of stringent multi-step annotation judgments, materially revising reliability and failure-condition discussions.

D1.justification: v2 specifies all-MiniLM-L6-v2 semantic embeddings and explains how existing scale labels partition expert training. The front-page link changes from a project homepage to a repository, and GWR collection and conditional release information are added. Conversely, the detailed QA prompt/answer examples and exact task-by-scene counts are removed. Most processing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware and generation settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds related-work citations including SpatialVLM, VLM-3R, Cambrian-1 and AutoFly, while dropping references associated with removed comparisons, such as NVILA and LongVILA. The central positioning around previously indoor-focused spatial reasoning and the claimed all-scale contribution remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendix structure is substantially condensed: retained observation sections are integrated into Model Detail, several statistics sections disappear, and the full QA Preview section is removed. The abstract and conclusion are edited, application discussion is recast as an Impact Statement, and acknowledgements and navigational lists are added.

P2.justification: The main paper switches to a two-column layout, with redesigned overview/pipeline graphics and extensively repositioned displays. Module and modality ablations are merged, the expert-count table is expanded, and a GWR table and image montage are added. Numerous diagnostic, detailed-comparison and QA-example displays are removed; retained appendix figures are resized and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new RL control, six-expert failure case and GWR stress test improve component attribution and scrutiny of generalization. However, v2 removes granular benchmark comparisons, training/router diagnostics and worked QA specifications, while changing benchmark size and model scores without explaining their relationship. These gains in analysis and losses in auditability leave the overall quality direction uncertain.
